To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
interface dynamics is a new paradigm for biological patterning and that it can be used to understand the mechanism of segmentation of Drosophilae.

the mechanism of size regulation in the segmentation process of the fruit fly Drosophila is a consequence of the interaction of kink domains of gene expression and that this mechanism bears analogy to the interface dynamics in condensed systems.

(i) the interface dynamics method is applicable to the segmentation of D. melanogaster, (ii) interface-kink interactions can explain the spatial distribution of genes and (iii) gene interactions can be used to predict interface-kink interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
interface dynamics in condensed matter physics and its application to developmental biology.
the development of new methods to study robustness in biological pattern formation.

the following questions: How can a gene network control robust patterning? How can a gene interaction scheme ensure the control of proportions? What is the role of interfaces (kink) in the patterning?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism of size regulation is based on kink-kink repulsion.
the proposed mechanism provides the simplest possible explanation of the observed size regulation.
the mechanism of size control is robust and that the mechanism of interface dynamics is the key for the control of proportions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
interface dynamics in gene networks can be used to control the spatial patterning of gene domains.
the gene network controlling the segmentation of D. melanogaster is a minimal network that ensures size regulation through kink-kink repulsion.
interface dynamics is a new concept for robust biological patternning and size regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kink-kink interaction can be calculated from gene-gene interaction, and that kink-kinks interaction can ensure the control of proportions.

the interface dynamics of the gene interactions is the key to understanding the robust spatial patterning in Drosophila and that the interface dynamics is controlled by a balance of weak and strong gene-gene interactions.
the interface between two kinked domains can be treated as a single entity and that the dynamics of such an entity is governed by a simple interface dynamics equation.
